notes: base_commit is the worktree HEAD before the first commit of this order (54b77779e4). The pin tree is detached at the release pin and was created outside the repository.

Evidence: IB193-1_digest_gate_stop.json read first. Each firm's moved members were recomputed from the three live bundles (get-object by version id, extracted to scratch outside the worktree) against the pin closure: the _IRPT_HOLDINGS_CLOSURE tuple parsed from the pin's .tools/safe_deploy_core.py, plus SHA256SUMS. The recomputed lists equal the evidence lists for every firm (49financial 19 content, 4 line endings, 1 added; cottonwood 21, 3, 1; inflection 20, 3, 1).
The live bundle metadata member-count reads 44 and the extracted tree holds 45 files (SHA256SUMS included); the pin closure holds 45 members plus SHA256SUMS. The metadata was not used.

Classes: line_endings where the CRLF-folded contents are equal to the pin's; docs where a .py parse tree with docstrings removed is equal to the pin's (one member, dim_mdpf_aggregate_aua_timeseries.py); data for lib/trading_calendar.py, the registries, NAMING_SCHEMA.json and the schemas; behaviour for other code, including the added opal_strategy_matcher.py.

live_commit is null for holdings_snapshot.py in all three firms: no commit in the file's history (71 commits searched from the worktree HEAD) carries the live folded hash. The three live copies also differ from one another. Every other changed member's live_commit is the newest commit whose folded blob matches the live member.

Reachability: the import graph among pin closure members (AST, function-level imports included, matched by module basename) and holdings_snapshot.py's BUILDERS table (49financial to build_49f_meshed, inflection to build_inf_meshed, cottonwood to build_cot). This is a static reading, not a runtime trace; each effect line names its call site.

Calendar: both modules were loaded from committed blobs (git show) by importlib, as the check does. pandas_market_calendars is absent in this environment, so both answered from the NYSE fallback and the module printed its WARN line on import. Neither module carries an early-close table. The window and the three fire dates are the order's.

Write addresses: lib/opal_naming.py address() was called with the arguments that publication.HoldingsPublication.location, land and write_refusal_record use, once under each firm's live bundle root (the bundle's own lib and registries) and once under the pin tree. Seven shapes per firm, with date normalised to date=* and revision to <revision>. The holdings_qa table is not written by production and was not enumerated.

Matcher: importer rebalancer_schemas.py (module-level import). build_cottonwood_mdpf_slice.py also imports the matcher inside a function. Both are on the cottonwood path only; the 49financial and inflection runs do not import the matcher.

Re-measure: release_count_harness.py ran read only from this worktree with the pin tree as repository root, --as-of 2026-10-12,inflection=2026-10-13 --firms all. Every count for every firm equals the signed packet's count. The pins block is the harness's pinned_as_of per firm.

Read-only AWS calls: three get-object calls by version id on the bundle keys (opal-data-49financial, opal-data-cottonwood and opal-data-inflection, each irpt/<firm>/code/gold/investor-reporting-holdings.tar.gz, derived with lib/opal_naming.py address()), and the harness's own get and list reads. No put, copy, delete, invoke, publish, sign-in or vendor call was made.
Not read: the current manifest versions of the three firms (the grant covers the bundle keys only). v1's manifest versions are carried in the packet as the recorded manifest anchors.

No account identifier, client identifier, position value, quantity or holding name appears in any tracked file. The harness's stdout (scratch only) names tickers and was not copied.
